key_insight: A question-type-specific LLM pipeline can improve biomedical QA by using different inference strategies for yes/no, factoid, and list questions instead of one uniform prompt.
clinical_relevance: Better answer robustness and evidence grounding could make literature-based biomedical QA more reliable for researchers and clinicians who need fast, accurate evidence summaries.
method: Yes/no: shuffled snippets plus self-reflection to reduce ordering bias and stabilize decisions.
Factoid: full-snippet input with chain-of-thought in-context learning for entity identification.
List: multi-agent workflow for evidence extraction, candidate generation, verification, and aggregation.
evidence_signal: The framework was tuned with preliminary BioASQ 13b experiments and then evaluated in the official BioASQ 14b Task B challenge, where it performed competitively and placed first in the factoid subtask of Batch 4.
watch_item: Performance is shown on BioASQ benchmark tasks, so real-world clinical deployment may still require validation for safety, generalizability, and citation reliability.
paper_title: From Voting to Agent Collaboration: Answer-Type-Aware LLM Pipelines for BioASQ 14b
